title: Tideglass v1 development backlog
effort_definition: Focused implementation person-weeks for the named primary contributor; reviews and other shared work use the unallocated capacity. These are planning estimates, not commitments.
capacity_assumption: Six full-time roles for a 36-week target, with 70% focus availability. Phase-role sums fit this envelope. Incremental handoffs in V1_ROADMAP.md are required; M0 must split packages into tasks and level their actual start dependencies. Strict finish-to-start interpretation of all links would have a 59.2-week lower bound before resource conflicts.

items.title: Define the release contract
items.acceptance: Freeze audience, iOS/Android scope, English launch, six-chapter content budget, ethical constraints, device targets and decision owners.

items.title: Qualify engine and numeric approach
items.acceptance: Build the same deterministic purchase/reset case on both native targets; compare large-number candidates and record the engine decision.

items.title: Prove native service integrations
items.acceptance: Demonstrate sandbox purchase/restore, ad availability and cloud revision handling in a throwaway integration build; list SDK and account dependencies.

items.title: Prototype the player journey
items.acceptance: Clickable flows cover first purchase, Rechart preview, offline return and recovery; identify accessibility and small-screen constraints.

items.title: Set visual production budget
items.acceptance: Approve one harbor look, one producer milestone transformation, asset reuse rules and a complete asset manifest.

items.title: Create quality and device plan
items.acceptance: Name reference devices, severities, reproducible save fixtures, test recruitment plan and the release evidence checklist.

items.title: Establish delivery and operating costs
items.acceptance: Confirm six role assignments, contractors, distribution accounts, tester recruitment and service cost model; reforecast for holidays and absences.

items.title: Create reproducible builds
items.acceptance: Automated builds run on both targets, version configurations and preserve build artifacts; no production secrets enter the client.

items.title: Implement production number handling
items.acceptance: Define precision, comparison and rounding rules; pass bulk-buy and prestige-boundary fixtures including extreme values.

items.title: Implement the economy state machine
items.acceptance: Five producers, unlocks, milestones, lifetime ledger and Rechart run without rendering; explicit event ordering is tested.

items.title: Build crash-safe local saves
items.acceptance: Atomic saves, rolling backups, checksums, export/import and versioned migration recover from interruption without double rewards.

items.title: Version configuration and content schemas
items.acceptance: Validate configs, pin economic versions to saves and provide safe defaults; reject incompatible updates before application.

items.title: Build the playable client shell
items.acceptance: Display wallet, output, producer purchases, milestones, resets and settings on small and large screens.

items.title: Design the full progression map
items.acceptance: Specify six chapter goals, ending, challenge entry requirements, Note source/sink budgets and daily/pass exceptions; no new prestige layer is assumed.

items.title: Produce reusable visual components
items.acceptance: Deliver modular producer parts, harbor layers, typography, icons and UI states sufficient for the slice.

items.title: Port oracle cases and failure fixtures
items.acceptance: Existing checks become production fixtures; add save corruption, rounding, rapid reset and interrupted-transaction cases.

items.title: Complete the first-session economy
items.acceptance: Cross-tier synergies, free autobuy unlock and baseline offline replay support first session through 25 Charts with deterministic results.

items.title: Build onboarding and Rechart communication
items.acceptance: Teach costs, production, retained progress and automation with skippable guidance; no monetization prompt interrupts onboarding.

items.title: Add purchase and reset forecasts
items.acceptance: Show marginal network output, next threshold and conditional reset estimate with readable assumptions and no claim of a universal optimum.

items.title: Implement optional cloud recovery
items.acceptance: Save revisions detect conflicts; divergent branches remain recoverable; never add two wallets or replay overlapping offline time.

items.title: Finish representative harbor presentation
items.acceptance: One area, all five base silhouettes and a milestone sequence establish final visual quality, including reduced-motion variants.

items.title: Run moderated first-session studies
items.acceptance: At least 15 new testers attempt the first reset; capture understanding, friction and pacing, then resolve the largest blockers.

items.title: Certify the vertical slice
items.acceptance: Replay purchase/reset/save/resume on reference hardware; publish a slice gate report and evidence for the next funding decision.

items.title: Implement all real-time boundaries
items.acceptance: 2-hour Focus, 8-hour Surveys, 24/72-hour offline envelope, bonus expiry and account-day boundaries resolve in a single event timeline.

items.title: Implement contracts and their backlog
items.acceptance: Seeded contracts, snapshots, offline progress, rerolls and 21-slot backlog preserve claim IDs and do not duplicate rewards.

items.title: Implement player automation plans
items.acceptance: Purchase priorities and opt-in reset conditions work identically online/offline; free base plan and Note-priced extra slots follow the blueprint.

items.title: Build calibration and daily interfaces
items.acceptance: Untimed calibration, equal-value accessible completion, queued Focus, Surveys and contract management form a complete daily session.

items.title: Complete settings and notification controls
items.acceptance: Text scale, number notation, motion/audio controls, input navigation and opt-in quiet-hour notifications function across targets.

items.title: Complete account lifecycle and branch recovery
items.acceptance: Guest linking, account recovery, export, deletion and divergent-save selection preserve recovery copies and purchased ownership.

items.title: Build the entitlement and claim ledger
items.acceptance: Unique receipts and idempotent grants separate cosmetics, Support allowance, pass XP and gameplay saves; interrupted grants resume safely.

items.title: Author chapter and challenge specifications
items.acceptance: Six chapters and twelve challenges have objectives, unlock rules, reward budgets and completion evidence; passive and active routes are covered.

items.title: Produce producer transformations and core UI art
items.acceptance: Five producer families each have base plus four milestone presentations; daily-loop icons and status states are final.

items.title: Validate the entire daily timeline
items.acceptance: Test 1/3/6 visits, 2/8/24/48/72-hour absences, clock changes, bonus queues and reset/day-boundary collisions; report exact and approximate differences.

items.title: Build reusable challenge scenarios
items.acceptance: Challenge state is isolated, goals are deterministic, main automation continues and exit/restart cannot export economic rewards.

items.title: Build the seasonal event state machine
items.acceptance: Season start/end/archive, event coefficients, pinned versions and offline transitions work; no paid or main-world power enters the event.

items.title: Build cosmetic shop and pass experience
items.acceptance: Preview, price, ownership, restoration, selected pass and archived completion are understandable; shared XP grants only once.

items.title: Integrate production purchase handling
items.acceptance: Validate, grant, acknowledge, restore and reconcile purchases; pending, duplicate, refunded and interrupted cases have explicit states.

items.title: Integrate optional ads and equal free rewards
items.acceptance: Ad and briefing routes consume the same allowance; no-fill, refusal and duplicate callbacks preserve access and cannot multiply rewards.

items.title: Finish all launch content and reward tables
items.acceptance: Six chapters, ending, twelve challenges, twelve calibration patterns, eighteen archive entries and Season 1 have complete data and copy.

items.title: Finish launch art and cosmetics
items.acceptance: Six harbor restoration states and the fixed 36-item cosmetic manifest are complete; commissioned audio is integrated through client work.

items.title: Verify content and monetization boundaries
items.acceptance: Every content ID and reward is reachable; full pass is completable free of paid speed; no event or cosmetic increases core power.

items.title: Optimize runtime and offline replay
items.acceptance: Meet measured frame/startup/resume budgets on minimum devices; heavy replay is chunked and never silently drops earned time.

items.title: Complete accessibility and language readiness
items.acceptance: Critical flows work at large text, without color/audio/motion dependencies and via target inputs; pseudolocalization has no blocking overflow.

items.title: Complete privacy and service recovery flows
items.acceptance: Data inventory matches SDK behavior; consent refusal, export/deletion and service-outage recovery are verified on actual builds.

items.title: Ship measurement and operating tools
items.acceptance: Validate economy/session events, entitlement dashboards, alerts, backups, support receipts and feature disable switches in staging.

items.title: Run long-horizon economy and content audit
items.acceptance: Simulate 30/90 days across visit and bonus policies, audit Note sinks and content pacing, freeze beta config and metric definitions.

items.title: Complete presentation and store assets
items.acceptance: Remove placeholders, integrate final sound direction, and prepare representative screenshots, icon and short footage.

items.title: Run device and migration regression
items.acceptance: Complete the device matrix, storage/network interruptions, upgrade migrations and install/return flows with zero open blocking issues.

items.title: Run commerce and service fault tests
items.acceptance: Purchase/restore/refund/ad callbacks are tested under packet loss, retries, duplicate messages, crashes and backend outages.

items.title: Recruit and freeze the measurement cohort
items.acceptance: Enroll the D30 cohort during week 27; record baseline config, acquisition source, denominator and exclusions before analysis.

items.title: Evaluate retention and content outcomes
items.acceptance: Report mature D1/D7/D30 with confidence intervals, campaign progress, bonus impact, satisfaction and explicit ship/change decisions.

items.title: Resolve economy and simulation findings
items.acceptance: Fix core bugs using replay fixtures; version any balance changes and keep affected cohorts separate.

items.title: Resolve comprehension and interaction findings
items.acceptance: Reduce observed onboarding/recovery friction without adding pressure, hidden rewards or paid advantages.

items.title: Operate staged access and support
items.acceptance: Exercise service load, support recovery, purchase reconciliation and feature disable controls with real opt-in testers.

items.title: Polish content from observed play
items.acceptance: Address readability, repeated visual issues and content defects without increasing the launch asset count.

items.title: Observe real calendar progression
items.acceptance: A real 28-day pass and mature D30 cohort are observed; accelerated testing is documented separately.

items.title: Rehearse season and release recovery
items.acceptance: Exercise season archive, paid pass continuation, save migration, purchase replay and compatible rollback/forward repair.

items.title: Decide readiness and freeze release scope
items.acceptance: Review all hard gates and product thresholds, assign accepted minor issues, and freeze the release candidate configuration.

items.title: Stabilize final game build
items.acceptance: Fix remaining blockers, tag deterministic core/config versions and prove candidate replay compatibility.

items.title: Package native release candidates
items.acceptance: Signing, install/update, responsive layouts, licensed assets and store-visible flows work in final distribution builds.

items.title: Prepare safe staged release
items.acceptance: Version-compatible config rollback, feature disables, capacity, backups and entitlement replay are rehearsed and documented.

items.title: Finish store communication and support material
items.acceptance: Screenshots, footage, credits, help visuals and release assets describe the actual shipped game and offers.

items.title: Approve the release evidence pack
items.acceptance: All gate evidence is linked; no blocker, save-loss, duplication or unresolved purchase-delivery issue remains.

items.title: Submit and manage platform review
items.acceptance: Recheck current platform requirements, provide reviewer access and working products, and resolve review findings before launch.

items.title: Hand over launch operations
items.acceptance: Document 14-day coverage, escalation, incident response and Season 2 preparation; launch authority and rollout stop conditions are explicit.

dependency_semantics: Acceptance prerequisites: listed packages must be accepted before the dependent package can be accepted. Work may start earlier against agreed interfaces, fixtures and content manifests. These links are not automatically finish-to-start scheduling constraints.
schedule_status: Milestone target with required intermediate handoffs; detailed sprint resource leveling pending M0.
